findings.issue_text: Websites that URI.parse rejects (e.g. URLs containing spaces like 'http://example.com/my page' or raw non-ASCII/IDN hosts like 'https://例え.jp') cause `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` to return nil, and since the template gates the entire block (icon + link) on `{{#if model.website_name}}`, the website row vanishes completely from the profile for those users — a silent regression, as the old `website.split("/")[2]` code still displayed these

Domain match is asymmetric: when the website host has more labels than the instance host (e.g. instance `example.com`, website `http://www.example.com/profile`), the elsif branch (equal label counts) and else branch (website host is parent of instance host) both fail, so only the bare host is displayed without the path — while the inverse case (instance `www.example.com`, website `http://example.com/profile`) correctly shows the path

Root path is not normalized: `URI("http://example.com/").path` returns "/", so a website of `https://example.com/` displays as `example.com/` with a trailing slash, while `https://example.com` displays as `example.com` — a cosmetic inconsistency from appending the raw path without normalizing "/" to ""

Entire `elsif` branch of `website_name` in app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:144-146 has zero test coverage: the equal dot-segment counts with >2 segments case (e.g. `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`) is never hit by any test, in either the positive direction (should return `www.example.com/user`) or negative direction (should return `www.example.com`)

Untested behavioral change: port (and userinfo) silently dropped from displayed website name — old frontend `website.split("/")[2]` displayed `example.com:8080` for `http://example.com:8080`, but the new serializer uses `URI(...).host` which excludes the port (same for userinfo like `user@example.com`), with no test documenting or pinning this change

No test for unparseable/scheme-less website values and the `include_website_name` interplay: for values `URI` can't parse or that yield no host (e.g. scheme-less `example.com`), `website_name` returns `nil` while `include_website_name` returns `true`, so the attribute serializes as `nil` and the template hides the entire globe/link block — also a behavioral change since the old `split("/")[2]` could still render text for some malformed inputs

Untested asymmetry: website as subdomain *of* the instance domain gets no full path — the mirror case of test 3 (website `forum.example.com`, instance `example.com`) falls to the `else` branch where `ends_with?(".forum.example.com")` fails, so only the bare host is returned with no path; if intentional, a pinning test is missing, if not, it's a bug the current suite cannot catch

Removed `websiteName` computed property without auditing other consumers: the user card template (user/card.hbs) may still reference `websiteName`, causing a silent cascade failure where Ember resolves the missing property to undefined, the `{{#if websiteName}}` guard evaluates false, and the website row vanishes from every user card with no exception, failed test, or log line; the PR must verify via grep that no remaining consumers exist or apply the same `model.website_name` treatment to the card

Website link silently disappears for values Ruby's `URI` cannot parse: `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` returns nil for unescaped spaces, raw non-ASCII, or control characters, so `website_name` is null while `include_website_name` still returns true, and the template guard `{{#if model.website_name}}` hides the entire website row — a silent regression from the old client-side `website.split("/")[2]` parsing which displayed these values; the guard should key on `model.website` or the serializer should fall back to a lenient parse

"Same domain" heuristic misfires on public suffixes and multi-level subdomains: branch 2's `split('.').length` equality plus `[1..-1]` suffix equality treats `evil.co.uk` as the same domain as `forum.co.uk` (co.uk is a public suffix, not a registrable domain) and likewise `a.b.example.com` vs `c.b.example.com`; the else branch's `ends_with?(".co.uk")` has the same flaw, causing the full URL path to be displayed for websites on completely unrelated domains; additionally branch 2 has zero spec coverage

goldens.comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Websites that URI.parse rejects (e.g. URLs containing spaces like 'http://example.com/my page' or raw non-ASCII/IDN hosts like 'https://例え.jp') cause `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` to return nil, and since the template gates the entire block (icon + link) on `{{#if model.website_name}}`, the website row vanishes completely from the profile for those users — a silent regression, as the old `website.split("/")[2]` code still displayed these

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the UI now renders the website section only when `model.website_name` is present (`{{#if model.website_name}}` in `user.hbs`). `website_name` is computed server-side via `website_host = URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` and returns `nil` when parsing fails (host `nil`). Even though `include_website_name` is true whenever `website.present?`, a parse-rejected URL will still yield `website_name: nil`, causing the entire website row (icon/link) to disappear. Previously the client-side `websiteName` used `website.split("/")[2]`, which would still show something for many malformed URLs, so this is a silent regression exposed by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Domain match is asymmetric: when the website host has more labels than the instance host (e.g. instance `example.com`, website `http://www.example.com/profile`), the elsif branch (equal label counts) and else branch (website host is parent of instance host) both fail, so only the bare host is displayed without the path — while the inverse case (instance `www.example.com`, website `http://example.com/profile`) correctly shows the path

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, the logic only appends the path when `website_host == discourse_host`, when the hosts share the same parent domain with equal label counts (>2) (the `elsif`), or when the instance host ends with `"." + website_host` (website host is a parent of the instance host). For the opposite case (website host is a subdomain of the instance host), e.g. `discourse_host = "example.com"`, `website_host = "www.example.com"`, the `if` and `elsif` fail and the `else` condition `discourse_host.ends_with?("." << website_host)` is false, so it returns only `website_host` (no `URI(...).path`). The inverse case (`discourse_host = "www.example.com"`, `website_host = "example.com"`) does include the path via the `else` branch. This asymmetry is directly implied by the diff and likely unintended given the intent to show the path for same-site domains.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Root path is not normalized: `URI("http://example.com/").path` returns "/", so a website of `https://example.com/` displays as `example.com/` with a trailing slash, while `https://example.com` displays as `example.com` — a cosmetic inconsistency from appending the raw path without normalizing "/" to ""

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, the code returns `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path` in several branches (e.g. when `website_host == discourse_host`, or when the instance domain is a subdomain of the website). If the user enters a website like `http://example.com/`, `URI(...).path` will be `'/'`, producing `example.com/`, while `http://example.com` would produce `example.com` (empty path). The diff shows no normalization of `'/'` to `''`, so the cosmetic inconsistency described is a real behavior exposed by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Entire `elsif` branch of `website_name` in app/serializers/user_serializer.rb:144-146 has zero test coverage: the equal dot-segment counts with >2 segments case (e.g. `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`) is never hit by any test, in either the positive direction (should return `www.example.com/user`) or negative direction (should return `www.example.com`)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial branching logic in `UserSerializer#website_name`, including an `elsif` branch for the case where `website_host.split('.').length == discourse_host.split('.').length` and that length is > 2 (e.g. `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`). The added specs only cover: (1) different domains (`discourse.org` vs `example.com`), (2) exact same host (`example.com` vs `example.com`), and (3) instance host being a subdomain of the website host (`forums.example.com` vs `example.com`). None of these hits the equal-segment-count >2 branch, so that branch currently has no test coverage. This is a concrete, diff-grounded missing-test issue rather than a proven functional bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Untested behavioral change: port (and userinfo) silently dropped from displayed website name — old frontend `website.split("/")[2]` displayed `example.com:8080` for `http://example.com:8080`, but the new serializer uses `URI(...).host` which excludes the port (same for userinfo like `user@example.com`), with no test documenting or pinning this change

adjudication.rationale: The diff moves `websiteName` from the frontend (previously `website.split("/")[2]` in `controllers/user.js.es6`, which would include port/userinfo like `example.com:8080` or `user@example.com`) to the backend serializer (`website_name` in `user_serializer.rb`) using `URI(...).host`, which drops port and userinfo by definition. The added specs cover domain/path variations but do not document/pin behavior for URLs containing ports or userinfo, so this is a specific, diff-grounded untested behavioral change rather than a clearly incorrect defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test for unparseable/scheme-less website values and the `include_website_name` interplay: for values `URI` can't parse or that yield no host (e.g. scheme-less `example.com`), `website_name` returns `nil` while `include_website_name` returns `true`, so the attribute serializes as `nil` and the template hides the entire globe/link block — also a behavioral change since the old `split("/")[2]` could still render text for some malformed inputs

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `website_name` computed in `UserSerializer#website_name` via `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` and includes it whenever `website.present?` (`include_website_name`). From the diff alone, it’s true that scheme-less/unparseable values can yield `website_host.nil?` → `website_name` returns `nil` while `include_website_name` still includes the attribute, and the template now gates display on `{{#if model.website_name}}` rather than computing a fallback from `model.website`. However, whether such malformed website values are possible/allowed is not shown in the diff, so it’s best treated as an untested edge case/incomplete handling rather than a definitively introduced defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Untested asymmetry: website as subdomain *of* the instance domain gets no full path — the mirror case of test 3 (website `forum.example.com`, instance `example.com`) falls to the `else` branch where `ends_with?(".forum.example.com")` fails, so only the bare host is returned with no path; if intentional, a pinning test is missing, if not, it's a bug the current suite cannot catch

adjudication.rationale: The new `website_name` logic in `user_serializer.rb` only appends the path when (a) `website_host == discourse_host`, (b) sibling subdomains with same label count and same parent (`www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`), or (c) when the *instance* host ends with `"." + website_host` (website is parent of instance, e.g. `forums.example.com` vs `example.com`). The mirror case mentioned in the finding—`website_host = forum.example.com`, `discourse_host = example.com`—does fall through to the final `else` and returns just `website_host` (no path). The added tests cover the parent-of-instance case but not this subdomain-of-instance asymmetry. Whether it’s a bug is not specified by the diff, but the untested edge-case in newly added nontrivial logic is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removed `websiteName` computed property without auditing other consumers: the user card template (user/card.hbs) may still reference `websiteName`, causing a silent cascade failure where Ember resolves the missing property to undefined, the `{{#if websiteName}}` guard evaluates false, and the website row vanishes from every user card with no exception, failed test, or log line; the PR must verify via grep that no remaining consumers exist or apply the same `model.website_name` treatment to the card

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes `websiteName` from `controllers/user.js.es6` and updates `templates/user/user.hbs` to use `model.website_name`. It does not show `user/card.hbs` (or any other consumer) still referencing `websiteName`, so the claimed remaining reference and resulting silent failure cannot be verified from the provided diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Website link silently disappears for values Ruby's `URI` cannot parse: `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` returns nil for unescaped spaces, raw non-ASCII, or control characters, so `website_name` is null while `include_website_name` still returns true, and the template guard `{{#if model.website_name}}` hides the entire website row — a silent regression from the old client-side `website.split("/")[2]` parsing which displayed these values; the guard should key on `model.website` or the serializer should fall back to a lenient parse

adjudication.rationale: The diff moves website display logic from client-side `website.split("/")[2]` (controller `websiteName`, removed) to server-side `UserSerializer#website_name`, which does `URI(website.to_s).host rescue nil` and returns nil when `URI()` can’t parse the string. The template now guards on `{{#if model.website_name}}` (changed from `{{#if websiteName}}`), so any unparsable-but-present `model.website` will result in `website_name` being nil and the website block disappearing. `include_website_name` only checks `website.present?`, so this mismatch can occur and is a behavior regression introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: "Same domain" heuristic misfires on public suffixes and multi-level subdomains: branch 2's `split('.').length` equality plus `[1..-1]` suffix equality treats `evil.co.uk` as the same domain as `forum.co.uk` (co.uk is a public suffix, not a registrable domain) and likewise `a.b.example.com` vs `c.b.example.com`; the else branch's `ends_with?(".co.uk")` has the same flaw, causing the full URL path to be displayed for websites on completely unrelated domains; additionally branch 2 has zero spec coverage

adjudication.rationale: In `UserSerializer#website_name`, branch 2 treats two hosts as “same domain” when they have the same number of labels and their suffixes excluding the first label match: `website_host.split('.')[1..-1] == discourse_host.split('.')[1..-1]`. This will classify `evil.co.uk` and `forum.co.uk` as related (both suffix `co.uk`) and return `website_host + path`, showing a full path for an unrelated domain. The same logic misclassifies multi-level subdomains like `a.b.example.com` vs `c.b.example.com` (suffix `b.example.com`). The spec additions cover branch 1 (exact match) and the else-branch “parent domain” case, but provide no coverage for branch 2.
